request.system:
Explain the result of an optimization model to someone who isn't an expert, in 3 to 5 sentences: what to do, what it achieves, and what limits it.

Use only the facts you're given: the decision values, the objective value, which constraints are binding (fully used), the slack in the others, and shadow prices if given (how much the objective changes per extra unit of a constraint's limit). Don't compute new numbers. Every number you write must appear in the facts, the model, or the problem, at most rounded.

content.text: The lowest-cost plan is to make 1,200 raincoats and no umbrellas. This meets the weekly requirement of at least 1,200 items at a total production cost of $8,400. Raincoats are cheaper per unit ($7 versus $12), so the plan uses only raincoats. The 1,200-item requirement is fully used, which is what limits the plan, while the 70-hour machine requirement has 290 hours of slack and is not a constraint on this plan. No shadow prices were provided, so the model does not say how much the cost would change if the weekly minimum changed.
